answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks via proof-of-identity (PoI), requiring complex computational work to mint each unique agent ID. This PoI, like refining digital copper, is computationally expensive, creating a high barrier to entry. Each verified ID is secured in a cryptographic vault. An attacker attempting to generate numerous fake identities would face prohibitive energy and resource costs, making even a zephyr of a large-scale attack economically infeasible.
